key_insight: A hybrid deterministic and LLM-agent translator converts quantum MLIR dialects to QIR, using dual-backend testing to detect translation errors.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce hand-written compiler work when connecting new quantum dialects to QIR runtimes while retaining deterministic translation for known grammars.
method: Use deterministic translation for Catalyst and Quake, and LLM agents for unseen dialects or repair after failed testing.
Run source MLIR and generated QIR on independent simulators; compare output distributions using total variation distance (TVD).
Support smaller open-weight models with inline context and a guardrail assembler that reconstructs valid QIR from incomplete output.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 tested circuit–dialect pairs with average 1−TVD above 95%; four of six models generated valid logical-level QIR for an unseen FTQC dialect on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR and close simulated output distributions do not alone establish semantic correctness for arbitrary unseen dialects.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
